newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Seng Bank remains soft after results.
newsitem.headline: Hang Seng Bank remains soft after results.

text.p: Shares in Hang Seng Bank Ltd remained soft after the bank reported disappointing growth in 1996 earnings, but downside was seen limited, brokers said.
The stock eased HK$0.50 to HK$84.25 in late Wednesday morning on volume of 2.21 million shares.
Brokers said the market was disappointed by the bank's higher bad debt provision at first glance and that triggered light follow-through selling.
Hang Seng Bank reported a 6.3-percent growth in 1996 net profit to HK$8.49 billion.
Some analysts said they saw a limited downside on the stock.
"We expect the shares to have a limited downside after the market discounted the bad debt concern," said Ricky Tam, senior analyst at Delta Asia.
"We maintain our hold recommendation on the stock due to its encouraging future prospects and we will recommend accumulate if the stock falls below HK$83," Tam added.

Fion Cheng, analyst at Tai Fook Securities, expected a solid profit growth on the bank in the longer run on its strategy of shifting to higher-yield assets from lower-yield interbank lending which would lift its net interest margin.
Hang Seng bank is a unit of HSBC Holdings plc.
